pros-cons-block-in-question.question:
D1 — Who receives the email when a task is assigned? <gstack-qid:spec-notify-recipients>
Project/branch/task: main branch, speccing "email notifications when a task is assigned to someone".
ELI10: Right now nobody gets told when a task lands on their plate. The obvious fix is to email the new assignee, but assignment also matters to the person who lost the task and to whoever created it. Each extra audience adds templates, preference toggles, and tests, and emailing people who do not care trains them to ignore your mail.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Too narrow and reassigned work silently vanishes from someone's queue. Too broad and your notifications become spam that users filter out.
Recommendation: A because the assignee is the one person who must act, and the other audiences can be added as a follow-up issue once the pipeline exists.
Completeness: A=7/10, B=9/10, C=10/10
Pros / cons:
A) New assignee only (recommended)
  ✅ One template, one recipient, one preference flag; smallest surface to test and ship (human: ~1 day / CC: ~10 min)
  ✅ Matches what every major tracker does by default, so users will not be surprised
  ❌ On reassignment the previous assignee is never told the task left their queue
B) New assignee plus previous assignee on reassignment
  ✅ Closes the "task silently disappeared" gap that causes duplicated work
  ✅ Still a small audience; two templates instead of one (human: ~1.5 days / CC: ~15 min)
  ❌ Requires reading the old assignee before the write, which constrains where the hook lives
C) Assignee, previous assignee, and task creator or watchers
  ✅ Full visibility for everyone with a stake in the task
  ✅ Lays groundwork for a general watcher model later (human: ~3 days / CC: ~30 min)
  ❌ Highest spam risk and needs per-audience opt-out from day one
Net: You are trading a small gap on reassignment against the cost of more templates, more preferences, and more inbox noise.
